note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received on Wednesday 20 April 1927; the Mid-Ulster Mail printed the full list of nominations by division (23 April 1927, p. 5), as did the Northern Whig (21 April 1927, p. 7). Killeenan, with two Nationalist nominations, was the only division polled, on Wednesday 1 June 1927, Tyrone's polling day for county council and rural district elections that year; every other division had one nomination. Labels are as printed. Killeenan was contested by two Nationalists, Mr. Michael M'Gurk and the sitting member, Mr. James M'Cracken, who had represented the division for 28 years. Polling took place at Gortacladdy School on Wednesday 1 June 1927; the presiding officer was Mr. William James Glasgow, clerk of the Union, and Mr. M'Gurk was declared elected by a majority of 110 (Mid-Ulster Mail, 4 June 1927, p. 8). No total poll or spoiled papers are printed.
